articles.title: Squid Game Increased Netflix's Value by Almost $1 Billion While Its Creator Received Virtually Nothing
articles.summary: A new report details how Squid Game creator Hwang Dong-hyuk lost the rights to his creation, which has made Netflix close to $1 billion.
articles.body:
Squid Game creator Hwang Dong-hyuk has been candid about his creation, which was a smash hit for Netflix in 2021, didn't make him rich. But it seems like it goes much deeper than that.

A new Los Angeles Times report details how Squid Game raised Netflix's internal value by some $900 million. Hwang, however, forfeited all intellectual property rights and received no residuals. In short, Squid Game belongs to Netflix now.

What does that mean for Hwang? In a 2021 interview, he said that Squid Game made him enough to put food on the table on top of suddenly being famous, but he's far from rich. Netflix, meanwhile, now has full control over one of the biggest franchises in the world.

Hwang spent a decade trying to sell his story, which was one reason he was so eager to sign a contract with the streaming giant. He was living with his mother and grandmother and at one point had to sell his $675 laptop to raise money. Netflix finally picked up the show, but in return Hwang forfeited all rights and royalties to what would become one of the streamer's biggest shows ever.

Hwang's story was used to illustrate a broader trend in which Netflix has profited from Korean dramas while the creators make very little.

"At first it was exciting to think that people all around the world would be able to watch my shows," a writer reportedly told the LA Times. "But now I'm thinking, 'So what? I'm not getting anything out of it."

According to the report, residuals are typically negotiated through the Korea Television and Radio Writers Association, but Netflix has no agreement with the group. Instead, writers typically receive their money up front, with rates starting at around $30,000 and going as high as $150,000. Shows can take between two to three years to create, but writers receive no more money in that time.

Netflix responded in a statement to the LA Times, "We pay fair, highly competitive rates with our K-Content creators and set clear standards for our Korean production partners, who produce all our shows and movies. These standards meet or exceed Korean law."

Netflix also claimed that its investments in the Korean film industry have created employment for "thousands of people locally."

One way or another, Squid Game continues to roll on. Earlier this week, Netflix revealed the new and returning cast for the show's second season, with the controversial reality show set to launch in November. Season 2 will be "bigger in scale" and will thus take longer to complete than the first , actor Lee Jung-jae has said. Hwang is also returning to work on Season 2, which he teased back in 2022.

Squid Game Season 2 does not yet have a release date.

Kat Bailey is IGN's News Director as well as co-host of Nintendo Voice Chat. Have a tip? Send her a DM at @the_katbot.

articles.title: How to Read The Witcher Books in Order
articles.summary: Here’s how to read The Witcher books in order that Netflix's Henry Cavill series is based on.
articles.body:
Before the award-winning RPGs or live-action show , there was The Witcher book series. Andrzej Sapkowski's original story of Geralt of Rivia was heavily inspired by Slavic mythology as well as classic fantasy series like Lord of the Rings . Whether you already enjoyed Netflix or CD Projekt's The Witcher adaptations or are just looking for a great book series, this wild world is worth diving into.

1. The Last Wish (Short Story Collection)

2. Sword of Destiny (Short Story Collection)

4. The Time of Contempt (The Witcher Saga #2)

5. Baptism of Fire (The Witcher Saga #3)

6. The Tower of Swallows (The Witcher Saga #4)

7. The Lady of the Lake (The Witcher Saga #5)

The first book in the saga, Blood of Elves, introduces Nilfgaardian Emperor Emhyr var Emreis’ pursuit of Ciri, Geralt’s adopted daughter, in order to marry her and attain power over Cintra, the land that is hers by birthright. In an effort to thwart Emhyr’s plans, the Northern monarchs meet and decide to assassinate Ciri, but Geralt of Rivia watches over her in Kaer Morhen, the remote keep inhabited by Wolf School witchers. Meanwhile, a mysterious sorcerer is also trying to locate Ciri.

The Time of Contempt picks up where the previous novel finishes. The Northern Kings are still conspiring with one another in an effort to lure Nilfgaard into war, while Ciri is due to be enrolled at Aretuza in order to study magic. Ciri comes into contact with some of the most powerful sorceresses on The Continent. As war becomes inevitable, she finds herself on the run with a bandit group known simply as The Rats.

Geralt spends time in Brokilon forest recovering from events in the previous book, which is where he and Dandelion encounter an elven archer named Milva, who decides to join their group. People who have played the games will be glad to know that the dwarf Zoltan Chivay temporarily joins Geralt’s ragtag group too, as well as the vampire Regis. A Nilfgaardian knight named Cahir also tags along because he feels indebted to Ciri. Geralt officially receives his “of Rivia” title after an epic battle while Ciri begins to feel at home with The Rats.

Ciri is gravely injured after an encounter with Nilfgaardian bounty hunter Leo Bonhart, who was hired by the coroner Stefan Skellen to kill her. A kind old man nurses her back to health while Geralt’s party continues their search for Ciri and Geralt renounces his status as a witcher. The Lodge of Sorceresses attempt to gain control of a country called Kovir while Triss Merigold seeks information on Yennefer of Vengerberg. (Known as The Tower of Swallows in the U.S.)

Ciri encounters Arthurian knight Sir Galahad who believes she is the eponymous lady of the lake. The story cuts to a dream in which Geralt overhears Skellen and sets out to rescue Yennefer from a faraway castle. Ciri, meanwhile, tells Galahad about her time in the elven world of Aen Elle, home of the Wild Hunt. She begins to jump between worlds in order to escape them, but Eredin Breacc Glas persistently chases her, as she heads towards a final meeting with her surrogate parents Geralt and Yennefer.

The most recent addition to The Witcher book series was published in Poland in 2024 before getting an official English translation in 2025. Out now , Crossroads of Ravens is a prequel that follows Geralt's "first steps" as a Witcher. The novel takes place before any of the original Witcher stories, making it the earliest on a chronological timeline. Still, as the most recent release, Crossroads of Ravens assumes some familiarity with the rest of the series, and is likely best enjoyed with knowledge of what's to come in Geralt's Witcher career.

Where Do The Witcher Games Fit on the Timeline?

The Witcher book saga starts roughly 10 years before the games, with most of the books' plotlines wrapped up by the time the first Witcher game starts. So, for those curious, playing the games first does mean you get some of the book series spoiled. That said, both the books and the video games are fantastic (we specifically called The Witcher 3 "Amazing" in our review ), so whichever one you start with shouldn't affect your overall enjoyment. Though the author himself has taken issue with some

Between the books, video game franchise, and TV series, there's a lot going on in the world of The Witcher. Netflix's live-action The Witcher series wrapped up its fourth season in 2025 featuring Liam Hemsworth as Geralt, but production on season 5 has hit a bit of delay recently and been pushed to 2027 .

If you're a fan of the Witcher III: Wild Hunt, there's a surprising new expansion due out in 2027 you can check out. Titled Songs of the Past , the new DLC is expected to arrive in 2027, almost 11 years after the second expansion released.

Of course, the big question is when we'll get another Witcher game. While CD Projekt has spent the past couple of years focused on Cyberpunk 2077, in early 2024, they proclaimed that the " bulk of its effort " is now going toward The Witcher 4 . The new game was officially announced with a cinematic trailer at the 2024 Game Awards . We don't have a release date yet, but The Witcher 3's active community is making the wait a little bit easier.

In a recent interview with IGN , Andrzej Sapkowski and his interpreter have confirmed that his next Witcher book is scheduled for 2027 .

articles.title: Microsoft is selling off four Xbox studios as part of significant gaming cuts
articles.summary: Double Fine and Compulsion Games are going independent, and Microsoft is also selling Ninja Theory and Undead Labs.
articles.body: Microsoft is laying off 4,800 employees today, and more than 30 percent of the job losses are in the company’s Xbox division. The significant gaming cuts will affect nearly every part of Xbox and also involve four game studios being spun off to be run independently from Microsoft. Today’s layoffs, which are being described as an Xbox “reset” moment, will impact around 1,600 Xbox employees, according to an internal memo from Xbox CEO Asha Sharma. The cuts won’t end today, though, as Microsoft is planning to eliminate a total of around 20 percent of Xbox jobs by the end of the financial year in July 2027. Double Fine and Compulsion Games are returning to their founders, so Tim Schafer will take Double Fine back to independence along with Guillaume Provost making Compulsion Games an indie game studio again. Ninja Theory, the maker of Hellblade, and Undead Labs, the developer behind State of Decay, are also being sold, with agreements in place to ensure Senua and State of Decay 3 continue to ship. “I recognize that a year-long restructuring creates additional challenges. Unfortunately, it is not possible to make all the necessary changes in a single day, and I wanted to be direct about the scale,” says Sharma. “I know this is painful. These changes will directly affect people who have poured their creativity into building Xbox. Many joined us through acquisitions, while others were recruited here, or sought us out because they loved this industry and loved Xbox. Today’s decisions do not reflect their talent or dedication.” Microsoft is also weighing up selling or closing another Xbox studio, as I reported last week. Arkane Studios is currently working on Blade under Xbox management, but the project has been delayed and is running over budget. “In France, Arkane’s management is beginning required consultation with its Works Council to review potential strategic options,” says Sharma. These discussions could take months, so it’s not clear what will happen to Blade or Arkane Studios just yet. Other Xbox studios will also be impacted by layoffs across the board, and I understand there are larger cuts to Bethesda studios in particular. As part of the studio changes, Minecraft maker Mojang and Candy Crush developer King will both now report directly to Sharma. “These changes vary in size across Activision, Bethesda/ZeniMax, Blizzard, King, Mojang, and Xbox Game Studios,” says Sharma. “None of our first party publicly announced games or projects are being cancelled as part of these reductions.” Today’s cuts at Xbox look like they’re targeted at reversing some of the smaller studio acquisitions that former Xbox chief Phil Spencer made in an attempt to compete more with Xbox Game Pass. Microsoft now appears to be aligning around bigger franchises, instead of trying to compete with indies with titles like South of Midnight, Kiln, and Keeper. “We now find ourselves competing not only with the largest publishers, but also with smaller independent studios,” says Sharma. “It is neither possible nor desirable to own every great independent studio. We have also learned that we are not the best home for every type of studio; in a typical year, we lost 64 cents for every dollar we invested. As we reset Xbox, we will help independent creators succeed by providing open development tools and audiences to realize their vision.” Here’s Sharma’s full memo: > Team, > We are beginning the most significant restructure in XBOX history. After careful consideration, I’ve made the difficult decision to reduce our team by approximately 3,200 throughout FY27. This will include approximately 1,600 role eliminations today, and in addition, four studios will leave XBOX to new management. I recognize that a year-long restructuring creates additional challenges. Unfortunately, it is not possible to make all the necessary changes in a single day, and I wanted to be direct about the scale. > I know this is painful. These changes will directly affect people who have poured their creativity into building XBOX. Many joined us through acquisitions, while others were recruited here, or sought us out because they loved this industry and loved XBOX. Today’s decisions do not reflect their talent or dedication. > Our business today is not healthy. We are operating at margins that are 3-10x lower than comparable platform and publishing businesses. We entered Gen 9 with a smaller install base and a higher cost structure. To grow, we bet on Game Pass, multi-platform, and a broader portfolio of content. While those businesses have created meaningful value, they did not grow at the pace we expected. As that happened, our core business weakened, and we added more teams, more investment, and more time, hoping for a better outcome. And now the industry is facing the most severe hardware crisis in its history. We must reset XBOX. First, we will reset our content portfolio. > Since 2018, we have aggressively expanded our studio portfolio while the number of games created each month across the industry now outpaces the last ten years combined. We now find ourselves competing not only with the largest publishers, but also with smaller independent studios. It is neither possible nor desirable to own every great independent studio. We have also learned that we are not the best home for every type of studio; in a typical year, we lost 64 cents for every dollar we invested. As we reset XBOX, we will help independent creators succeed by providing open development tools and audiences to realize their vision. > Compulsion Games and Double Fine Productions will return to management and transition to independent studios with their IP, catalog, and runway for their next games. Ninja Theory and Undead Labs have entered terms to join new ownership with funding to complete and grow Senua and State of Decay 3. In France, Arkane’s management is beginning required consultation with its Works Council to review potential strategic options. > We are also making reductions across other units, and in some cases, shifting investment to focus on higher priority projects. These changes vary in size across Activision, Bethesda/ZeniMax, Blizzard, King, Mojang, and XBOX Game Studios. None of our first party publicly announced games or projects are being cancelled as part of these reductions. > In addition, Mojang and King will now report directly to me. These two studios have increasingly become platforms and are our largest by monthly active players. They bring critical geographic, demographic, and differentiation to XBOX. > Second, we will reset our platform. > We know that great technology gets better when it gets simpler, not bigger. Today, in some parts of the company, work passes through as many as 14 layers of management. Our platform teams are 40% larger than they were at the start of this generation, even as our player base and playtime have declined. That complexity has slowed decisions, blurred accountability, and made it harder to deliver for players. As we reset XBOX, we will simplify. > We will reduce management layers to no more than 5, and where possible, 3. We will deliver success through a flatter organization that is built around makers (individual contributors focused on building), player-coaches (leaders who remain deeply involved in the work while developing their teams), and directly responsible individuals (DRIs) who own key decisions and outcomes. And we will streamline how we work across our tools, with a cleaner code base, shared services, and 50% reduced vendor spend. > Third, we are resetting how we operate. > As XBOX grew our headcount, we became more fragmented. Teams, studios, and functions often operate independently, and it became harder to work towards a shared goal, make the right tradeoffs, and get things done. > For the first time, we are establishing a Chief Operating Officer with end-to-end P&L responsibility across content, hardware, platform, and services. Helen Chiang has been promoted to this role and will report directly to me. Over nearly two decades at XBOX, Helen has helped build some of our most important businesses, from XBOX Live to leading Mojang and the Minecraft franchise. She will bring our businesses together under one operating model, making sure we make clear investment decisions, learn from our successes and failures, and hold ourselves accountable for results. > Thank you, Dave McCarthy, who is retiring after 17 years with XBOX. Dave has played a defining role in building the platform that millions of players rely on every day and has been a trusted partner through many of the biggest moments in XBOX’s history. We wish him all the best. > These changes are about a bigger future for XBOX, not a smaller one. The next decade of gaming will be larger, more global, and more creative than anything we’ve seen before. This year, we’ll invest as much in XBOX as we ever have, but we’ll invest with greater focus, greater discipline, and greater clarity, all in service of making XBOX where the world plays and creates. > I want XBOX to be one of the few companies that entertains more than a billion people each day and gives everyone the opportunity to create and connect. I know we can achieve this goal. XBOX has many of the most beloved franchises in entertainment history, talented studios around the world, and we will return to growth in 2027. > History is full of companies that mistake longevity for inevitability. We will not be one of them. > Asha Update, July 6th: Article updated to clarify Xbox’s layoff percentages for the fiscal year.

articles.title: Nvidia RTX 6080 Reportedly Delayed to 2028, According to Leaker
articles.summary: The next-generation Nvidia graphics cards have reportedly been delayed to 2028, according to known Nvidia leaker Kopite7Kimi on Twitter.
articles.body:
We're nearly two years out from the RTX 5090 launching at CES 2025 , and if everything was normal, Nvidia would likely be getting ready to release its next generation of graphics cards at CES 2027, but it doesn't look like that's going to happen.

The next-generation Nvidia graphics cards, likely based on the Rubin architecture, have reportedly been delayed to 2028, according to known Nvidia leaker Kopite7Kimi on Twitter . This isn't the first time Nvidia has been reported to either delay or cancel a graphics card in the last year, either. Back in February, the same leaker suggested that Nvidia's typical mid-generation Super refresh was also canceled, thanks to increased demand for GPUs and memory for AI data centers.

I hope Jensen can see everyone's passion and launch new products for gaming as soon as possible. Unfortunately, GR20x is a product from 2028. That means they have postponed again. 🙃🙃🙃 I will try to minimize updates until there is definite news. (Lessons learned) — kopite7kimi (@kopite7kimi) September 21, 2026

I hope Jensen can see everyone's passion and launch new products for gaming as soon as possible. Unfortunately, GR20x is a product from 2028. That means they have postponed again. 🙃🙃🙃 I will try to minimize updates until there is definite news. (Lessons learned)

It is important to keep in mind, though, that leaks for Nvidia's next-generation graphics cards are all over the place. Just last week, YouTuber Moore's Law is Dead cited nebulous sources inside Nvidia, suggesting that the Rubin-based RTX 6000 graphics cards would be launching sometime in the first half of 2027.

You should take both of these leaks with a grain of salt, but Nvidia delaying its next-generation graphics cards to 2028 would make a lot of sense. After all, the flagship GeForce RTX 5090 is now commanding prices around $9,000 , despite launching for $1,999 last year.

The RTX 5090 isn't the only GPU going up in price, either. We're now 10 months into RAMageddon, and it's unlikely to end any time soon. Thanks to that ongoing shortage, every graphics card on the market is much more expensive now than it was a year ago. Even without that happening in the background, Nvidia would probably raise the price on its next-generation graphics cards, but now that memory and GPU costs have gone through the roof, I shudder to think how expensive the RTX 6080 would even be.

Nvidia has also dropped the gaming category from its earnings reports, lumping GeForce in with the 'Edge Computing' category, along with robotics. In its recent Q2 2027 earnings report, Nvidia didn't even mention gaming, instead focusing on the mountains of money it's making from AI. So, Team Green is likely also in no rush to get new consumer graphics cards out there.

Only time will tell whether or not Nvidia has anything up its sleeves for gamers next year, but if it's anything like 2026 so far, we're likely just going to get more software tricks – not that that's necessarily a bad thing.

articles.title: Daredevil: Born Again Will Reportedly End With Season 3, Showrunner Departs Amidst Post-Production
articles.summary: Daredevil: Born Again will reportedly end with its upcoming third season.
articles.body:
Daredevil: Born Again will reportedly end with its upcoming third season.

According to The Hollywood Reporter , Daredevil: Born Again will not return for a fourth season. Disney reportedly made the decision following the end of production on the third season, suggesting the show wasn't necessarily designed to end here. Additionally, THR reports that the Marvel series' showrunner, Dario Scardapane, exited the project during post-production. Sources reportedly raised eyebrows at the departure, as it has left the show without a clear leader to finish it. Daredevil: Born Again Season 3 is currently expected to premiere in 2027.

It's unclear if Daredevil: Born Again was canceled or if it truly is just the end of this story. The series wasn't a smash hit when it came to ratings, but was hailed as a success by critics and fans, especially compared to other Marvel shows. Disney has pulled back on Marvel TV series in recent years following a string of mediocre releases, but is still committed to a small handful moving forward. The next Marvel show will be VisionQuest, releasing on October 14. THR also noted that three to five other shows are in development, including a spy series named Zodiac.

Wonder Man was also canceled earlier this summer , despite getting greenlit for a second season. As of right now, it's unclear what Daredevil's future is in the MCU. Fans have wanted to see him in a film, especially after his brief cameo in Spider-Man: No Way Home. As Spidey continues to embrace street-level battles, a Daredevil crossover in the next film could be extremely fruitful.

This is also the second time the Man Without Fear has had his TV time cut short at the third season. Netflix and Marvel pulled the plug on the original Daredevil series in 2018 following a critically-acclaimed third season. A fourth season was expected to follow, but various issues prevented that from happening, such as Disney trying to launch its own streamer with original programming. It took the better part of a decade to get Daredevil back on screen, but fans were excited once it finally happened, particularly because it continued the story of the original show and leveraged its darker tone.

Is this the end of Matt Murdock's journey in the MCU? Only time will tell, but we hope that's not the case.

articles.title: Rockstar Games Is Taking Down Footage and Images of Scrapped GTA 5 DLC And Early Version of Leaked GTA 6 Map
articles.summary: Take-Two Interactive, the parent company of Rockstar Games, has begun taking down videos and posts about leaked GTA 5 and GTA 6 content.
articles.body:
Take-Two Interactive, the parent company of Rockstar Games, has begun taking down videos and posts about leaked GTA 5 and GTA 6 content.

Last week, a ton of files for Grand Theft Auto 5 leaked online. These were reportedly obtained during the 2022 hack, which also resulted in the first-ever footage of GTA 6 leaking online. These files have been rumored for some time, but are only just now surfacing publicly. They include cut dialogue from GTA 5, which also seems to hint at different outcomes for the story, such as a darker ending for Franklin. However, the two biggest things are details of a scrapped Liberty City expansion for GTA 5 and an extremely early version of GTA 6's map.

Given that this material was illegally obtained in a hack and not officially released by Rockstar or datamined through the game's files, the studio's parent company, Take-Two Interactive, is working to scrub the assets from the internet. Various YouTube videos and posts with visuals of the leaked material or clips of the audio have been taken down by Take-Two. It doesn't seem like the company is going scorched-earth like it did for the GTA 6 leaks, but it does appear that content creators who post this material are at risk of copyright strikes.

We're just two months away from the release of GTA 6, and it's likely that Rockstar's security is going to be at an all-time high. The studio has been compromised by multiple leaks for the last four years, and now it's at a point where the game is likely finished and could be at risk of being spoiled. However, the lack of physical copies will make it a lot harder for things to leak ahead of its release. Given tons of footage managed to surface in August , though, it's not impossible for more things to make their way online.

articles.title: Bloodborne Movie Reveal Reactions Were '80% Critical,' Jacksepticeye Says
articles.summary: Bloodborne movie producer and YouTuber Jacksepticeye has teased more details about the upcoming animated adaptation after reactions to his involvement were "80% critical."
articles.body:
Bloodborne movie producer and YouTuber Jacksepticeye has teased more details about the upcoming animated adaptation after reactions to his involvement were "80% critical."

The famed content creator, whose real name is Seán McLoughlin, touched on his attachment to Sony's animated take on FromSoftware's beloved action game during an interview with 100 Questions with Tom Simmons (via GamesRadar ). He took the opportunity to not only tease how his Bloodborne won't retell the story of the franchise's one and only proper installment, but also discussed how fans reacted to his role as its producer.

"Bloodborne, obviously, is my favorite game ever, so when I got that call, part of me is like… obviously I was going to do anything, but I wouldn't have let it go in a direction that I don't think is worthy of the Bloodborne IP," Jacksepticeye explained. Then, when asked if he was feeling the pressure to deliver, he said, "Oh yeah."

"I'd say 80% of the responses were critical of it," he said, referring to his involvement in the animated film. "I don't want to say 'negative,' because a lot of people were just… I would be the same if someone took my beloved IP, that's my favorite, and then some YouTuber's attached to it. It would just make you scratch your head a little bit."

Sony unholstered its plans for an animated R-rated Bloodborne movie back at CinemaCon 2026 in April. For some, the reveal was a bit of a double-edged sword, as begging to see more from FromSoftware's Lovecraftian action-horror universe seemed to deliver a project that came out of left field in more ways than one.

Jacksepticeye, a self-proclaimed Bloodborne fanatic, is in the mix as one of its producers. He's joined by PlayStation Productions and Lyrical Animation. Shortly after its reveal, the YouTuber called the opportunity "a dream come true" and "the honor of my life."

He also acknowledged that a lot of Bloodborne fans were probably surprised to hear his name attached to an official project in that universe. Regardless of the shock, it's not a project he wants anyone to be worried about, saying that he "will fight tooth and nail to make this thing the best it possibly can be."

When asked during the new interview about what fans can look forward to when it comes to the animated movie, Jacksepticeye assured watchers that he's "not trying to be the game."

"I'm not trying to one-up the game, and I'm not trying to compete with it, or tell the same story," he explained. "I'm trying to honor the universe that's there and tell as good a story as I can within it."

He continued, saying he has "quite a bit" of sway in the overall production and direction of the Bloodborne movie. During calls about the project, he said that "people listen to me above most anyone else."

"I'm the one being like, 'This is a good idea. This is a bad idea. We shouldn't do this,'" Jacksepticeye elaborated. "But also, I'm the one greenlighting who gets hired and who we work with to make sure that vetting process is good.

"You don't want to bring on anyone that has no idea what Bloodborne is. In simpler terms, I'm sort of the vibe-checker."

The Bloodborne movie currently has no release date. While we wait to learn more about it, you can check out IGN's original 9.1/10 review of the game. You can also read more about Jacksepticeye's approach to the film .

articles.title: Call of Duty YouTuber Launches Petition to Remove Skill-Based Matchmaking Following Successful Destiny Protests
articles.summary: Call of Duty YouTuber Tdawgsmitty has started a petition to remove skill-based matchmaking in the FPS franchise following successful Destiny protests.
articles.body:
Call of Duty YouTuber Tdawgsmitty has started a petition to remove skill-based matchmaking in the FPS franchise following successful Destiny protests.

The YouTuber has been an outspoken advocate against Call of Duty's SBMM and has tried to make noise on the issue in a variety of ways. Last week, he began tweeting at Xbox CEO Asha Sharma about the matter every day in hopes of getting her attention. Now, he's trying a different way. After seeing Destiny fans successfully rally together to get Bungie to resurrect the sci-fi MMO, Tdawgsmitty decided to try to bring Call of Duty fans together in hopes of a similar outcome.

The YouTuber launched a petition which has gained over 500 signatures in roughly an hour. The call to action aims to get SBMM entirely removed from Call of Duty's unranked lobbies, citing frustrations with the current system and how Activision uses data analysts to develop its matchmaking. Instead, he wants the series to utilize SBMM in the game's ranked play, where players deliberately choose to have a more competitive experience.

"Former Call of Duty developer Brian Bright recently shared that his team’s work on [the canceled Call of Duty game NX1] focused on ping and region," reads the description for the petition. "He also stated that Activision eventually began hiring data scientists who worked with its marketing department to push for more skill-based matchmaking. His statement raises serious questions about how matchmaking priorities evolved.

"For players like us, today’s public matches too often feel like the same competitive experience on repeat. Experimenting with a different weapon, relaxing after work, or playing with friends of different skill levels can become frustrating. When every lobby feels like another test, the fun starts to disappear."

The YouTuber also asked for clearer communication regarding matchmaking and the opportunity for the community to test changes itself. The petition comes roughly a month ahead of Modern Warfare 4's release, which will utilize a divisive SBMM system that was introduced earlier this summer in Black Ops 7. Some feel that Call of Duty's SBMM is too punishing and can result in matches that feel consistently unfair, leading to years of frustrations about the franchise's multiplayer.

Whether a petition can change the mind of Activision remains to be seen, but it's not entirely out of the question. Bungie opted to return to Destiny 2 after killing it earlier this year. There was extreme backlash to the initial decision and players decided to make their voices heard through online protests, which included players choosing to not support Bungie's latest game, Marathon. The developer announced that it will be restoring vaulted content and plans to keep supporting the Destiny franchise, leading to an enthusiastic response from fans . Tdawgsmitty cited this as proof that change is possible.

"This Destiny news is huge for gaming," he said on Twitter . "It shows we can use our voice and effect change. It's time for the COD community to step up and get some much needed changes to the direction its been headed."

If Call of Duty fans can rally together by signing petitions, making their voices heard online, and vote with their wallet, it may very well lead to changes. However, Call of Duty is a massive franchise, and as a result, it may be difficult to make the same kind of dent. IGN spoke with Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4's lead multiplayer developers in August and asked about how the studio is approaching SBMM.

"I think it's a conversation that we'll continue to have," said Jacky Reynolds, Multiplayer Design Lead at Infinity Ward. "I don't think it's ever going to be a solved system. There's always going to be new iterations that can be made. I think at the end of the day, yeah, we want players to be able to play and have fun. I think that we want to also make sure that they have variety in their matches. I think it's a conversation that we should continue to have. It's also worth mentioning that Joe and I aren’t directly in charge of matchmaking. We are focused on building cool stuff, but I think we're looking forward to seeing how it all shakes out."

Cade Onder is a freelancer for IGN's news team. He covers all things entertainment, including gaming, film, and more. You can find him on Twitter @Cade_Onder.

articles.title: Love Nikki Player Shuts Down Fan Website Over Game's 'Irreverent' and 'Demonic' Clothing Designs
articles.summary: A fan of the Love Nikki – Dress Up Queen mobile dress-up game is going viral for shutting down their informative website after determining that some of the game’s clothing designs were “demonic.”
articles.body:
A fan of the Love Nikki – Dress Up Queen mobile dress-up game is going viral for shutting down their informative website after determining that some of the game’s clothing designs were “demonic.”

Nikki’s Info was a fan-made website compiling many of Love Nikki’s clothes, accessories, story guides, update details, and other information. An X/Twitter account for the site was created in 2018, and players could subscribe to the administrator’s Patreon for exclusive game guides and other insights.

Those players are now being offered refunds after the site’s admin announced that they are quitting the game due to their religious beliefs, as described in a now-viral blog post .

The admin published the post after a week of inactivity on the Nikki’s Info website, which has been completely wiped of any information relating to the dress-up game. They explained their absence in the post, saying they had “done some horrible things involving the occult” and that the “devil had then gained such a foothold in my life [that] I was firmly in his grasp.”

“All of this started quite small and personal — but quickly escalated, where in the end I was in a situation where I was in a near-death situation involving police, paramedics, and other people, of whose kindness I am grateful for. I [was] on the precipice of a terrible situation — [I] called out to God for help. He answered. I then continued to practice the occult. Things got worse again and started affecting others, especially my suffering family, in a way I can’t declare publicly,” they wrote.

While the poster confirmed that they are now fine, they expressed some issues with the clothing designs in Love Nikki, finding them to be blasphemous with “demonic” undertones.

“The game features a lot of crosses as dress-up items, which are irreverent to God, the God who so kindly and patiently saved me. The God I love,” they continued. “There’s a lot of them, disproportionately so. Some are mixed in with gothic demonic themes. Such things, though they might seem small, carry consequences and meaning. This is not to say that playing the game directly led to what happened to me. I can say with some degree of certainty, it really was the terrible things I did. But in the ‘back story,’ the various games, books, works of fiction, movies, even music — they are there.

“I have wrestled with this, but ultimately I can’t profit from or promote something which offends my God, my Saviour — therefore the site is now closed. The source code, the data, the domain are not for sale.”

⭐Behind the Seams | [Version 2.0 5-Star Outfits] The Inspirations Behind the Designs pic.twitter.com/KMOoKqvo67 — Infinity Nikki (@InfinityNikkiEN) December 10, 2025

⭐Behind the Seams | [Version 2.0 5-Star Outfits] The Inspirations Behind the Designs pic.twitter.com/KMOoKqvo67

The admin’s post has gone viral within the broader Infinity Nikki community, sparking concerns from players and theories as to what clothing items specifically led them to this conclusion.

Some pointed out the oddness of the situation, given that a fair few designs within the Nikki franchise were directly inspired by figures within the Catholic religion. For example, Love Nikki includes an outfit set that’s essentially a Pope-like ensemble, while the official Infinity Nikki X account shared a graphic with specific details about how the team at Infold approached its Behind Prayers outfit set, saying the Starlight Crown headdress incorporated “imagery of the Virgin Mary.”

For now, commenters are doing their best to help the Nikki’s Info admin, though the situation has sparked no end of curiosity and debate within the world of dress-up games.

articles.title: The Blood of Dawnwalker Update to Add Easier Difficulty Setting for Players Who Don't Want Combat
articles.summary: The first major The Blood of Dawnwalker update will introduce an easier difficulty option for "people who don't want to experience combat" when it launches in October.
articles.body:
The first major The Blood of Dawnwalker update will introduce an easier difficulty option for "people who don't want to experience combat" when it launches in October.

Developer Rebel Wolves' game director, Konrad Tomaszkiewicz, teased the changes coming to the team's breakout vampire RPG during a new interview with Eurogamer . Amongst a batch of combat tweaks and other gameplay changes, one of the highlights for the early October The Blood of Dawnwalker update includes reworked difficulty options for players who don't want to spill too much blood during the story.

When the update launches, players will see the new easier difficulty option replace the current easiest mode, called Story Mode, and adopt its name. The version of the mode currently in the game will seemingly be bumped up a peg and given a new name. The Blood of Dawnwalker currently has four difficulty modes – Story, Fair, Challenging, and Duelist – with next month's addition set to bring the total to five.

"We will introduce an additional difficulty level, but an easier one, because many people are asking for a more easy difficulty," Tomaszkiewicz said. "The Story mode which we have right now will be a different difficulty — we will call it Demanding or something like this — and we will add a new Story mode which will be even easier for people who don't want to experience the combat, they just want to learn the story and go through the game without this gameplay challenge."

How exactly The Blood of Dawnwalker will tackle an easier difficulty mode is unclear. The game director's comment suggests it will cater to those who want to skip combat altogether, though how this will be achieved is unclear. There's no release date for the update just yet, but with its launch set for early October, we won't have to wait too long.

Rebel Wolves is also looking into improving gameplay performance, especially for PC users, as well as a fluid option for players to escape fights if they bite off more than they can chew. Other items on the docket include targeting and the camera. Tomaszkiewicz referenced desires from players to tweak how targeting works for Coen and how the upcoming patch will address that.

The Blood of Dawnwalker - Prologue Screenshots

"There will be three hits you need to take off this stun," he said. "We will see how people will react to that because, as I said, it can create another bad feel, but we will see. Maybe people will switch between targets fluently and if they want to just stun, it will be fine, and if they want to stun and hit a few times, it will be also fine. We will see."

Everything else set to come to The Blood of Dawnwalker in the October patch has yet to be revealed. Although other features, including new game plus , are confirmed to be in the cards, the team is still charging ahead following its successful launch.

It was released for PC, PlayStation 5, and Xbox Series X/S September 3 and reached more than 1 million copies sold in just two days . For more on The Blood of Dawnwalker, you can read about how Bandai Namco and Rebel Wolves managed to bring their vision to life on a $40 million budget . You can also learn about how some players are using a mod to bypass one of the game's core mechanics .

articles.title: IGN's StarCraft: Tabletop Miniatures Game Review
articles.body:
Long before I deployed my first army of little plastic figures on a table for war, I was mowing down the slithering Zerg and doing battle against the Queen of Blades in StarCraft. The term “Space Marines” I will now, and forever, associate with the Terran army from Blizzard’s classic RTS franchise (despite Games Workshop’s version being older and SC starting off as a 40K RTS). When Archon Studio, a board game developer with an impressive history of adapting massive games for the tabletop, announced they were making a tabletop miniature war game set in this universe, I started clearing off my hobby table in anticipation.

Similar to other tabletop war games, standard matches of StarCraft take place over the course of five rounds where players or teams struggle to complete objectives. Instead of picking one from a book, at the start of each game, players will bring two possible choices each for both what the game’s type (i.e. the goals both sides are working to complete) and deployment zones, which dictate where armies and objectives will be placed. From there, the choices are drafted, with one person picking the type and the other the deployment. It’s a system that I found not only works really well but adds to the variety of possible matches you experience. I’m also a big fan of the concept of players supplying the choices themselves, as everyone is submitting options that could benefit their side. The result of that ultimately means both sides will have to deal with a scenario that isn’t quite as ideal as they had hoped for.

In addition to their maps and mission cards, each player brings a host of other cards with them that help define the composition of their armies along with upgrades they have purchased. Faction cards, which are picked before the game, establish the number and variety of slots available in your army, such as how many core units (your basic troops), elites, or heroes (Raynor or Kerrigan, for example) you can include, along with some unique benefits or tags for that specific faction. These tags may be required when selecting which Tactical cards to buy, with these representing various buildings from the RTS games or perks that can impart special bonuses, buffs, or increase the number of supply slots available to your forces. Along with the fact that all the troops and their required information—stats, costs, everything you need to know—are included on handy info cards, I love that I don’t necessarily need to carry around a rulebook whenever I want to play. Instead, I can just throw a small deck of cards into my bag, which is incredibly convenient, and far lighter to carry around. And in practice, it’s really quick and easy to just hand the reference card to the other player if they have a question about an ability, as opposed to book-marking pages in a rule book or handing over a sheet with all the information that has to be parsed through.

When it comes to each of the three races’ minis, all of them come in a unique color plastic along with impressive semi-transparent accents that really help to make the models look great. Inside the Starter Set, Terrans feature a muted blue and include orange explosion effect pieces and green healing sprays for the medics, for instance, while Zergs are a pinkish-purple and Protoss a bright yellow with blue energy shields and blades. And yes, there is even a Pylon miniature with a large clear blue crystal, so you can build all the additional pylons you want! The models are impressively detailed and just begging for a sick paint job. Even if you just opt for a primer base coat and a wash, the model details along with the accent parts really help all the units pop and look great on the table.

StarCraft features a host of design decisions that make it a far more alluring prospect for me to play than other tabletop war games , largely thanks to keeping me more engaged and leaving me with far less downtime than 40k, which is where I have spent the most of my wargaming time. StarCraft adopts a system of alternative activations, meaning that I never have to worry about hour-long stretches of downtime as I wait for my friends to take their entire turn before I can act. From deployment, to moving, to shooting and close combat, the fact that I was never out of actively participating in the game for longer than a few minutes made me so much more invested and excited in games of StarCraft. It turns out that not having to try to remember a strategy you came up with an hour back before you can implement it is actually really nice!

The alternating turns is only part of what has really helped StarCraft win me over. Instead of deploying all (or most) of your troops at the very start, all units begin in reserve, with the battlefield only able to field a limited amount of troops at a time. This supply limit, dictated by the mission picked at the start, keeps things more manageable (and timely), with each unit on the field taking up various amounts of that given limit, with squads like the Terran Marines supply value reducing as they lose troops. Then at the start of a brand new round, that limit increases, allowing for fresh and stronger troops to deploy, with that limit removed altogether if the game lasts until the final fifth round. Not only do I appreciate this approach since it removes the likelihood of a disastrous first turn ruining your chances at the start of a long game, but I found it lets players adjust their strategies and approach better mid-game, as the deployment order of troops isn’t set until the moment they are taken out of reserve. So if you really need bodies on the board, you can change your strategy from bringing out your heavy units next round to a couple more squads of zerglings to swarm the field. It also feels more faithful to the original PC RTS , as you build up your army as the game progresses.

StarCraft’s twists don’t stop just at deployment or when you take your turn though, despite its combat feeling a bit familiar if you have played a tabletop war game before. Movement will still have you busting out your handy-dandy tape measure and combat is still a chaotic symphony of rolling handfuls of dice for attacks and defense. The twist the Archon Studio has thrown into the fighting pits is the Surge mechanic. Some weapons units come with a designated “Surge type” with an associated tag, such a “Light” or “Armoured”. When using that weapon against an enemy with a matching tag, some of your successful hits for damage will circumvent the opponent’s armor roll, and will deal damage. It almost turns encounters into a rock-paper-scissors game where there is a clear and impactful incentive to attack units with the right type of counter unit, and adds a satisfying and clever layer of strategy to battles.

One unfortunate carry over that StarCraft hasn’t managed to avoid, that plagues the hobby as a whole, is that this can still be a rather pricey game to play. The two player Starter Box which includes a Terran and Zerg army hovers around the $200, with individual army starter sets for Zerg, Protoss, or Terran will set you back $120-$130, with the various squad or hero boxes coming in between the $50 and $80 price point. It’s the world we live in, I suppose, but to Archon Studio’s credit, the full rulebook is available for free along with a handy browser app with the various cards you can use, so if you find yourself with some standard bases, some LEGO miniatures and super glue…

articles.title: One Fan's Rey/Kylo Ren Fiction 'Fixed' Those Characters, Only to Be Rewritten as a Book... and Now a New Movie
articles.summary: The Love Hypothesis review: Ali Hazelwood’s New York Times bestseller gets adapted into a charming rom-com.
articles.body:
The Love Hypothesis streams exclusively on Prime Video starting September 23.

Sometimes a rom-com isn’t just a rom-com; such is the case with The Love Hypothesis, a Prime Video movie adaptation of author Ali Hazelwood's 2021 New York Times bestseller. In most cases, that’s a cut-and-dry scenario. However, Hazelwood’s book evolved out of the author’s frustration with how the Star Wars sequels turned out; she, among many, was so frustrated with how the characters of Rey and Kylo Ren/Ben Solo were done dirty in Star Wars: The Rise of Skywalker that she “fixed” their outcomes through a creative outpouring of fan fiction. One of them was rewritten as The Love Hypothesis and published, turning into an international BookTok sensation and now a movie.

Why all the history? Because The Love Hypothesis has been created with a decidedly modern lens, depending on the audience watching it. For everyone who just enjoys an entertaining rom-com or loved the book, The Love Hypothesis is an accessible, charming watch led by the warm chemistry of the entire cast, especially leads Lili Reinhart and Tom Bateman. For anyone who comes to it from Star Wars fandom and has followed the journey of Hazelwood and her story to this moment in time, the movie is a very meta wink filled with easter eggs tailored just for them.

The basic story remains the same: Third-year Stanford University PhD student Olive Smith (Reinhart) is overworked and underfunded in the traditionally male-dominated science world. Her lifeline through it all is best friend Anh (Rachel Marsh), a fellow PhD student who has pulled Olive out of her shell, introduced her to other friends like Malcolm (Jaboukie Young-White), and become her ride-or-die found family. When Jeremy (Nicholas Duvernay), Olive’s one-time crush, shows interest in Anh, Anh won’t do anything about it because their girl code is stronger than mutual attraction. Olive lies that she has a new boyfriend to get Anh to pursue Jeremy, but that backfires when Anh wants in-person details about Olive’s “date,” and a panicked Olive kisses the first man she sees for cover — the departmental Kylo Ren, Dr. Adam Carlsen (Bateman). What starts as a horribly awkward moment becomes a mutually agreed upon ruse between Olive and Adam when he shares that his grant money is under threat of not being released. Stanford is worried that Carlsen is a flight risk to another research institution, so he could use a “girlfriend” to make it seem like he’s got roots and won’t be exiting anytime soon.

For both audiences, their public relationship-proving moments escalate into more awkward expressions of intimacy, such as suntan lotion applications and recounting their fictional “meet-cute” to his colleagues. Wisely, director Claire Scanlon ( The People We Hate at the Wedding ) allows these scenes to breathe, heightening their comedic potential and allowing the ensemble to bring out the laughs, of which there are many. Marsh and Young-White are particularly good at pitch-perfect reactions or zingers that lean into the silliness of the “fake dating” scenario while also building a little ecosystem of friendship that drives why Olive is doing what she’s doing.

Reinhart and Bateman also absolutely sell the thawing between these two socially awkward dorks into a genuine romance. Yes, in reality they’re both too pretty to ever have that descriptor applied to them, but as Olive and Adam, you buy why they’d hold the world at arms’ length and decide not to do so with one another. Comedically, they’re top notch, and the scenes where they get to express genuine honesty and mutual loneliness with one another percolates into a friendship and bubbling attraction that’s the do-or-die element to any great rom-com.

The STEM-centric aspects of the story are watered down in Sarah Rothschild’s script, though an homage sequence to Martha Coolidge’s 1985 science comedy, Real Genius, very much works as it adds a sense of color and context to Olive’s world. Less successful is the science villain of the piece, who gets a lot more time to unfurl his machinations in the book. Here, he isn’t given enough story real estate to be as potent an adversary, or to even rise above a one-note character with clichéd intentions. Fortunately, Rothschild’s screenplay replaces that screen time with more consequential scenes for Olive and Anh, the bedrock for why this “fake dating” operation is even happening. Portraying the strength of their bond is far more worthwhile, underpinning the romantic story with a deeper one about friendship and sisterhood.

And for the fans who go all the way back to this story’s Star Wars origins, there are a wealth of easter eggs to find and laugh over, from pointed needle drops to very specific Laura Karpman musical character themes, and even red-and-blue color cameos. The production knows who you are, and they’ve clearly got a sense of humor and respect for the OG fandom.

At its heart, The Love Hypothesis is a gentle satire of romance tropes, especially enemies-to-lovers, and a celebration of female friendship. Both sound potentially hokey, but this mostly female creative team understands what made the book a hit and knew how to translate it here. They let the tone be earnest yet firmly tongue-in-cheek, and allow their cast to weave their magic — especially Reinhart and Bateman — giving rom-com lovers the exact chemistry that makes the genre work.

articles.title: Injustice 3 Leak Reportedly Reveals 2 Playable Characters
articles.summary: Injustice 3 will feature one character fans will expect and one who perhaps comes as a surprise, according to a fresh leak.
articles.body:
Injustice 3 will feature one character fans will expect and one who perhaps comes as a surprise, according to a fresh leak.

MP1st unearthed evidence to suggest the unannounced fighting game will feature both Supergirl and Batwoman on its roster of playable characters. Supergirl comes as no surprise, given her starring role in the nine-year-old Injustice 2. But Batwoman’s inclusion — assuming it’s true — would mark the debut for the character in the mainline Injustice games.

Batwoman (Kate Kane) dies in the canon Injustice comics, which suggests someone else has taken up the Batwoman mantle for Injustice 3, Kate Kane didn’t actually die, or the game retcons the events of the book. Either way, this is a superhero story we’re talking about — no-one stays dead forever.

DC Universe: Every Upcoming Movie and TV Show

Or, as MP1st suggests, Injustice 3 may not continue the story told in Injustice and Injustice 2, but act as a reboot that tells an entirely different story. NetherRealm’s other fighting game franchise, Mortal Kombat, has done this multiple times, so it wouldn’t be a huge surprise with Injustice since it’s been nearly a decade since Injustice 2 came out.

Publisher Warner Bros. has yet to announce another Injustice game, despite it being an open secret at this point. Given Paramount looks like it’s finally going to get the green light to complete its $110 billion merger with Warner Bros., perhaps that will provide some clarity on the company’s video game plan, which we know also include Hogwarts Legacy 2 and a new Batman game from Arkham developer Rocksteady.

My guess is Injustice 3 — or whatever it’s called — is announced at The Game Awards in December, with a release set for in or around April 2027.

In May, NetherRealm development chief Ed Boon said another Mortal Kombat game was in development , which again, didn't come as much of a surprise. Confirmation of another Mortal Kombat game came after 2023’s Mortal Kombat 1 sold 8 million copies, just over half Mortal Kombat 11’s total of 15 million copies sold, as of 2022. Perhaps this new Mortal Kombat game will be released after Injustice 3.

The first game in the series, Injustice: Gods Among Us , launched in 2013, with its sequel, Injustice 2 , coming out in 2017. NetherRealm released Mortal Kombat 11 in 2019 and for a time it seemed like the studio would alternate between Mortal Kombat and Injustice games, but it went on to release another Mortal Kombat, the soft reboot that is Mortal Kombat 1, in 2023 instead.

articles.title: How Long Is Silent Hill: Townfall?
articles.summary: Five different IGN editors played through Silent: Hill Townfall in five different ways to find out how long Konami's new survival horror is, depending on playstyle.
articles.body:
Konami's latest game in the nu-Silent Hill era has arrived, and as is the case with previous entries in the series, Townfall boasts a handful of endings to unlock and an even bigger handful of scares. But how long does it all take? We got five different members of the IGN team, who all played Silent Hill: Townfall very differently, to share their time. So whether you’re a completionist, or just someone who’s only interested in the story, you’ll learn just how long you’ll be spending in St. Amelia depending on your playstyle.

Our fastest player finished Silent Hill: Townfall in 12 hours and 37 minutes.

Our “slowest” player spent 15 hours and 15 minutes before credits rolled.

Everyone plays games differently, so read on for more details about how everyone played, how long it took to reach the credits, and some of the individual statistics from their end-of-game report card. Once you've finished the game yourself, be sure to submit your times on How Long To Beat and see how your time compares!

Player: Jesse Gomez Completion Time: 12 hours and 55 minutes

With just under 34 hours of playtime under my belt, a few restless dreams between two separate playthroughs, and three wildly different endings, my intended aim was clear: to experience as much of Silent Hill: Townfall as possible.

To start, I chose the Normal/Hinted difficulty, which Townfall recommends when you select new game in the main menu. That combo set me up for a 12 hour, 55 minute clear time, reaching the "Forever" ending. As far as I could tell at the time, this was a largely "positive" outcome, but I knew there had to be more to unravel with a "true" ending, so to speak.

Once I hit New Game Plus, however, it became pretty clear that new collectables had snuck into this seaside town. I quickly abandoned Simon's hunt for the truth to instead get the bizarre secret endings, something that’s a Silent Hill tradition and well worth seeing for yourself. You can get both of these in the same playthrough with some additional puzzle-solving, combing over every inch of Townfall, and some tactical saving.

Despite experiencing true horror in the form of the auxiliary line B puzzle for nearly an hour, and pushing myself through a New Game Plus puzzle that had me on the verge of tears, I'm sure I could've cleared Townfall a lot sooner. But what's a Silent Hill game if not incredibly obtuse and wholly rewarding all at the same time?

Player: Matt Purslow Completion Time: 15 hours and 15 minutes

The fog-shrouded island of St. Amelia is the stage for a different kind of Silent Hill compared to what we’ve had over the past couple of years. Where the Silent Hill 2 remake was a traditional survival horror and Silent Hill f went heavy on the combat, Townfall features comparatively fewer enemies and far fewer options for eliminating them. As a result, combat is downplayed and each individual foe feels more like a mini “stalker” enemy than a regular mob. This design influenced my entire playstyle: for me, Townfall was a stealth game.

My slower, more cautious approach means I clocked up a slightly longer time compared to most of my colleagues – it took me 15 hours and 15 minutes to complete my first run of the story. Rather than bludgeoning every enemy with my pipe, I’d use bricks and bottles to distract them and create openings for myself. My final stats claim I spent four minutes and 15 seconds hiding, but that only accounts for when I was concealed in lockers – I spent many, many more minutes hiding behind cover or locked in sheds and bathrooms as I tracked enemies on the CRTV and planned my next move. I chose my victims carefully, only killing foes that blocked pathways I’d frequently use as I looped back and forth around each location. My total kill count was 76, most of them racked up when the pressure really kicks in during the story’s final chapters.

This approach netted me the “Abandoned” ending, which felt thematically appropriate for the story, but definitely leaves the door open for more discoveries. And so I’m looking forward to diving into New Game Plus to take another crack at solving St. Amelia’s troubles.

Player: Dale Driver - Story Mode Completion Time: 12 hours and 37 minutes

I really enjoy the stories of Silent Hill, particularly their ambiguity and puzzles, but I've been less engaged with their combat recently, so I decided to try Silent Hill: Townfall on Story Mode to make getting through fights a easier. With this set up I clocked a final time of 12 hours and 37 minutes, reaching the "Abandoned" ending.

In Story Mode, enemies drop a little easier, and there are more supplies in storage cupboards and drawers, so I found myself taking on more monsters than my colleagues did, clocking up a whopping 105 kills during my time in St. Amelia.

One thing Story Mode doesn’t help with, though, is the puzzles, and a few particular late-game ones really added significantly to my playtime. I found a few particularly obtuse (or maybe I was just being really dumb) but I could easily see a second playthrough taking half the time when you know the solutions. And I plan to do just that, knowing there are new weapons to find and four new endings to discover. After all, the story is what I love the most, so I can’t wait to learn more about it.

Player: Lauren Harper Completion Time: 15 hours and 8 minutes

It took me around 15 hours and 8 minutes to finish my first playthrough of Silent Hill: Townfall. As a member of the guides team at IGN, I always find that it takes me a bit longer than everyone else (my current overall play time shows 44 hours). I’m often writing while I play and taking screenshots of everything as I run back and forth, double-checking each drawer, cabinet, and locked room to make sure I don’t miss anything in terms of collectibles. That being said, I did actually miss a few of the 85 possible discoveries. What I didn’t miss out on was the opportunity to use every weapon in the game, and I racked up a kill count of 92. I also finished up with the "Abandoned" ending on my first go.

I then played through again and decided to take on as much of a pacifist run as possible. I avoided killing anything unless it was absolutely necessary and opted for a stealthier approach using every method of distraction I could find. Despite a more considered playthrough, because I knew all the puzzle solutions and locker combinations on my second go, my second run came in at 8 hours and 24 minutes, with just five saves, but an enormous number of healing items used. This netted me the "Justice" ending. Is this the "true" ending? You'll have to play to find out. Now, I’m off to complete another New Game Plus run to hunt down anything new and find those remaining collectibles so our guide is complete.

Player: Tristan Ogilvie Completion Time: 13 hours and 36 minutes

Given that I was reviewing Silent Hill: Townfall for IGN , I tried to be as thorough as possible with my search through the small town of St. Amelia and beyond. Playing on the Normal difficulty settings for both combat and puzzles, it took me 13 hours and 36 minutes from the moment Simon washed up on the Scottish shoreline through to the intense final moments of its climactic boss fight. Although admittedly, roughly 30 of those minutes were spent stuck on one of the late game puzzles that had me properly flummoxed. Curse you, auxiliary line B!

According to the endgame stats page, I made 78 out of the 85 discoveries and found 9 out of the 13 phone numbers, so clearly there was the odd optional room here and there that I overlooked. Although I spent much of the early hours opting for stealth and avoiding enemy confrontations, I still managed to murder 92 of Townfall’s ghouls by the story’s end, with the vast majority of those occurring in the second half of the game once more powerful weapons were made available. Ultimately, the ending I received was the one dubbed "Abandoned".

I definitely plan to do another run-through on New Game Plus, although it won’t be in the near future because trying to keep up with all the other awesome games coming out this month is a form of survival horror in itself.

articles.title: Here's Your First Look at 3 Cards From Pokémon TCG: Mega Evolution — Delta Reign, Due to Launch This November
articles.summary: IGN can today reveal three new Pokémon card designs from the upcoming set Pokémon TCG: Mega Evolution — Delta Reign.
articles.body:
IGN can today reveal three new Pokémon card designs from the upcoming set Pokémon TCG: Mega Evolution — Delta Reign.

Due to launch on November 6, this latest batch of Mega Evolution-themed cards includes creatures such as Mega Malamar, Mega Golurk and Mega Rayquaza, with over 135 designs in total.

Today, we can show off our first look at starter Sprigatito, the Grass Cat Pokémon, as well as both of its evolutions, Floragato and Meowscarada.

Pokémon TCG: Mega Evolution — Delta Reign Cards

Sprigatito's design shows the cute kitty settling down for a late morning nap on a trainer's bed. Its 70 HP is decent, though its Play Rough attack lacks a little punch.

It's lucky, then, that you can evolve Sprigatito into Floragato, with 90 HP and the Slash attack for a chunkier 60 damage. With that on the board, you're on your way to playing Meowscarada ex, which lands with a solid 320 HP and the strong Magical Bullet attack, that can deal a whopping 120 damage to its opponent, and another 120 damage to any damaged benched Pokémon. As with all ex cards, though, Meowscarada will count for two prizes if knocked out.

Pokémon TCG: Mega Evolution — Delta Reign will be the next set to launch following the current Pokémon 30th Anniversary release, which arrived last week to huge demand , queues , fights , and ultimately some disappointment from scalpers who haven't been able to turn their usual profits . Oh dear!

articles.title: The Legend of Zelda Movie Actress Posts Cryptic Tease, Raising Hopes for an Imminent Trailer
articles.summary: The Legend of Zelda movie star Bo Bragason has raised hopes of an imminent trailer release for Nintendo's upcoming film.
articles.body:
The Legend of Zelda movie star Bo Bragason has raised hopes of an imminent trailer release for Nintendo's upcoming film.

With just seven months to go until The Legend of Zelda arrives in theatres, Nintendo and Sony (which is distributing the film) are yet to show anything of it in motion. Sure, we've had a few photos of Bragason in costume as Zelda , alongside House of the Dragon actor Benjamin Evan Ainsworth as Link. But there has been no sign of a teaser, and still no official confirmation of the film's wider cast — despite many unofficial reports now having emerged.

Could all of that change today? Fans certainly believe so, as Bragason posted on Instagram last night to say she was "excited 4 tomorrow." Bragason regularly posts on Instagram about her upcoming projects, though has acknowledged she can say nothing specific at all about The Legend of Zelda, which Nintendo is keeping under lock and key.

Fans had hoped we'd see something more of the film in this month's recent Zelda-focused Nintendo Direct , but in reality there was little to add. Nintendo confirmed that The Legend of Zelda would be the movie's name, and acknowledged it would be an original story inspired by the franchise so far, rather than a direct adaptation of any particular game.

Originally announced in 2023, The Legend of Zelda is helmed by Maze Runner and Kingdom of the Planet of the Apes director Wes Ball, while Nintendo's legendary Shigeru Miyamoto is listed as a co-producer, alongside Marvel production veteran Avi Arad. The movie was shot last winter in New Zealand, with the Middle-earth-like location now doubling for Hyrule.

Unofficially, it's been reported that Dichen Lachman (Severance) will play Impa, while Uli Latukefu (Black Adam) will play Ganondorf. These will be joined by other castmates such as Yvonne Strahovski, Lydia Peckham and the late Sam Neill . While their roles have yet to be disclosed , Deadline reported that the former will be playing a "queen" character.

Could we see them confirmed officially today? Time will tell. But what we do know for sure is that The Legend of Zelda is currently set to arrive in theaters on April 30, 2027.

articles.body: Microsoft is reportedly planning to cut jobs in its Xbox division. Citing sources familiar with the company’s plans, The Verge reports that the company may lay off hundreds of employees later today. First reported by The Information, the layoffs will be the company’s second major staff reduction this year. Microsoft Xbox is also planning to consolidate many of its game studios, the report said. Earlier this year in July, Xbox CEO Asha Sharma told staff she would eliminate 1,600 roles by the end of the year on top of 1,600 roles the company cut that month. At that time, Xbox also sold four of its game studio subsidiaries.The layoffs and restructuring come as Sharma tries to improve profits at the gaming business, which has been behind some of its rivals. She has also asked Xbox to focus more on developing major game franchises such as Elder Scrolls and Fallout, while reducing its focus on smaller studios it bought in recent years.Asha Sharma took charge as Xbox CEO earlier this year. Soon after taking over, she moved quickly to change Xbox's business. Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella and CFO Amy Hood had earlier discussed restructuring Xbox or even separating it from Microsoft, The Information previously reported. However, they have more recently backed Sharma's plans to restructure the gaming business.Asha Sharma lays out four-point plan after 2,800 job cutsIn a memo sent on July 30, Xbox CEO Asha Sharma said the business will return to player and revenue growth by the end of fiscal year 2027, which wraps next June. Profits, she added, need to climb back in line with industry averages. Every function and every studio owns a slice of that outcome.Sharma then laid out four priorities for FY27, each starting with the letter C: strengthen the platform led by console, grow games into global franchises, turn Minecraft into a creator platform, and extend the worlds fans already love.Get the latest technology news and updates. articles.title: 'I'm Too Old': Marvel Star Says He's Officially Retired From His Beloved Guardians of the Galaxy Role as Rocket Raccoon
articles.summary: Marvel actor Sean Gunn has officially retired from his role playing Guardians of the Galaxy and Avengers hero Rocket Raccoon.
articles.body:
Marvel actor Sean Gunn has officially retired from his role playing Guardians of the Galaxy and Avengers hero Rocket Raccoon.

After five films and one holiday TV special, Gunn has said he's now "too old" to provide the performance capture for the beloved Rocket (whose voice is then dubbed in post-production by Bradley Cooper).

Speaking to podcast host Brandon Davis , the Gilmore Girls legend said he had made the decision to depart his role as Rocket after recently turning 50, and noticing that the amount of crouching he'd had to perform for the part was beginning to have an effect on his "physiology."

Behind the Scenes Photos from Guardians of the Galaxy

On set, behind the scenes footage has featured Gunn scuttling around the legs of his Marvel co-stars while squatting down in what he describes as a "catcher's crouch" position. Thankfully, Gunn could also stretch his legs and stand up to also play Kraglin, the Ravager who ultimately ends the sci-fi saga as a fully paid-up Guardians member.

"Everyone thinks it's my knees but it's really my feet and my ankles," Gunn said, describing the physical difficulty he has faced after portraying Rocket Raccoon. "Because I'm in a catcher's crouch and I'm pivoting a lot on my points of contact with the ground... I'm doing a lot of pivoting in my ankles and feet. And over the years I think it had a little bit of an effect on my physiology.

"My knees are fine but since I turned 50 a couple of years ago I am retired from Rocket," he admitted. "Not that they've called but if they did, I don't think I could do the motion reference for Rocket anymore. I'm too old."

When might we see Rocket again? It's hard to say. Marvel is yet to confirm its future plans for the Guardians of the Galaxy, which remains a hugely popular team of characters, though one whose story has reached a natural conclusion. Gamora is off with the Ravagers, Drax and Nebula are looking after an array of children, while Mantis has also gone off to find her own path.

Guardians of the Galaxy Vol. 3 ends with a new team forming, featuring Rocket, Groot, and Kraglin joined by Adam Warlock, Cosmo the Space Dog, and Phyla. It's unclear if any of the above characters will ever return to the MCU, and it seems unlikely we'll get another Guardians of the Galaxy movie any time soon, with its writer and director James Gunn (yes, Sean Gunn's brother) now heading up the DCU. But Marvel has promised that Chris Pratt's Star-Lord will appear at some point (our best guess would be in Avengers: Secret Wars).

But even if Rocket Raccoon is invited back for the Multiverse Saga's big finale, it'll be someone else who squatted down to portray him instead.
